steps.tx: Fractures of the metacarpals and phalanges require precise anatomical alignment to prevent functional impairment. Any **rotational deformity** in a finger fracture is unacceptable: with fingers flexed into the palm, all normal fingertips point toward the scaphoid tubercle. Five degrees of rotation causes 1.5 cm of digital overlap.
steps.say: In the finger, rotation is the unforgivable deformity. Ask the patient to make a fist and every fingertip should converge on the scaphoid tubercle at the wrist; just five degrees of twist at the fracture makes the finger scissor over its neighbour by a centimetre and a half.

nodes.label: Assessment of flexion cascade pointing to scaphoid tubercle
Any scissoring or digital overlap mandates anatomical reduction

steps.tx: A **boxer fracture** is a fracture of the fifth metacarpal neck, resulting from an axial blow on a clenched fist. Because the fourth and fifth carpometacarpal joints possess 20 to 30 degrees of compensatory sagittal mobility, up to 40 degrees of volar apex-dorsal angulation is tolerated without surgical intervention.
steps.say: The boxer's fracture breaks the neck of the little-finger metacarpal after a punch. Because the outer two knuckle joints at the wrist flex and compensate through twenty to thirty degrees, up to forty degrees of forward bend can be left to heal in a cast without surgery.

right.title: Ring/Little Metacarpal
points: Tolerates up to 30 to 40 degrees angulation

steps.tx: Intra-articular thumb base fractures comprise Bennett and Rolando fractures. A **Bennett fracture** is an oblique intra-articular fracture-subluxation where the volar anterior lip fragment remains attached to the beak ligament, while the abductor pollicis longus pulls the main shaft proximally, radially, and dorsally.
steps.say: At the thumb base, a Bennett fracture splits off the small volar lip, which stays tethered by the beak ligament, while the big thumb tendon drags the whole shaft outward and upward into subluxation. That two-part pattern usually needs screws or wires to hold the joint surface true.

vis.alt: Surgical reduction clamp for thumb metacarpal fracture
vis.caption: Surgical instruments for anatomical reduction of hand articular fractures. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: A **Rolando fracture** is a comminuted intra-articular T-shaped or Y-shaped fracture of the base of the first metacarpal. Because of severe comminution and joint disruption, Rolando fractures carry a poorer prognosis and are managed with open reduction and low-profile plate fixation or dynamic external fixation.
steps.say: A Rolando fracture is the Bennett's ugly cousin: the same thumb base shattered into a T or Y with the joint surface in pieces. Comminution and joint disruption give a worse prognosis, so open the joint and rebuild it with a miniature plate or a dynamic external fixator.

left.title: Bennett Fracture
points: Closed reduction and percutaneous K-wire pinning

right.title: Rolando Fracture
points: Both volar and dorsal articular fragments
Open plate osteosynthesis or external fixation

steps.tx: Injury to the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint is known as gamekeeper or **skier thumb**. Laxity exceeding 30 degrees of valgus opening or 15 degrees greater than the uninjured side indicates complete rupture, requiring prompt surgical evaluation to rule out a displaced Stener lesion.
steps.say: Skier's thumb is a tear of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb knuckle when the ski pole wrenches it open. Stress the joint sideways: more than thirty degrees of opening, or fifteen degrees more than the good thumb, means the ligament has fully ruptured and needs an operation.

steps.tx: A **Stener lesion** occurs when the torn ulnar collateral ligament retracts and becomes trapped superficial to the adductor pollicis aponeurosis. Interposition of the aponeurosis physically prevents spontaneous ligament healing to the bone, making open surgical repair or bone anchor reattachment mandatory.
steps.say: A Stener lesion is what makes that rupture irreparable by splinting. The torn ligament end flips out and lies on top of the adductor aponeurosis, which then sits between the ligament and its bony home, so no scar bridge can ever form without opening the thumb to tuck it back.

nodes.label: Hyperabduction force ruptures UCL from proximal phalanx base
Torn ligament end flips superficial to adductor pollicis aponeurosis
Interposition blocks contact with bone, demanding open repair

steps.tx: Dorsal proximal interphalangeal joint dislocations are frequently accompanied by **volar plate avulsion** fractures. If the volar articular fragment involves over 40% of the middle phalanx articular base, the joint becomes unstable, predisposing to recurrent dorsal subluxation that requires extension block splinting or hemi-hamate arthroplasty.
steps.say: When the middle finger joint dislocates backward it often tears off the volar plate with a chip of bone. Below forty percent of the joint surface the joint stays stable, but a bigger fragment lets the joint keep slipping backward, calling for an extension-block splint or a hemi-hamate graft.

vis.alt: Surgical instruments for ligament and bone anchor repair
vis.caption: Precision instrumentation for small joint ligamentous reconstruction. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Splinting of hand fractures must maintain the **safe position** of immobilisation (intrinsic-plus position): wrist in 20 to 30 degrees extension, metacarpophalangeal joints flexed to 70 to 90 degrees to stretch the collateral ligaments, and interphalangeal joints fully extended to prevent joint contractures.
steps.say: Every hand injury must be splinted in the safe intrinsic-plus posture. Extend the wrist twenty to thirty degrees, bend the knuckles to seventy or ninety so the collateral ligaments heal at full stretch, and keep the finger joints straight, because a collateral ligament that heals short is a contracture for life.

rows: Prevents volar plate and collateral ligament contracture
